cue_isometric_chest_squeezes_1: While either seating or standing, bend your arms at a 90-degree angle and place the palms of your hands together in front of your chest.
cue_isometric_chest_squeezes_2: Push both hands against each other as you contract your chest. Start with slow tension and increase slowly.
cue_isometric_chest_squeezes_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.
cue_isometric_neck_exercise_front_and_ba: With your head and neck in a neutral position (normal position with head erect facing forward), place both of your hands on the front side of your head.
Now gently push forward as you contract the neck muscles but resisting any movement of your head. Start with slow tension and increase slowly.
Using heavy momentum instead of squeezing the upper back.
cue_isometric_neck_exercise_sides_1: With your head and neck in a neutral position (normal position with head erect facing forward), place your left hand on the left side of your head.
cue_isometric_neck_exercise_sides_2: Now gently push towards the left as you contract the left neck muscles but resisting any movement of your head. Start with slow tension and increase slowly.
cue_isometric_neck_exercise_sides_mistak: Using heavy momentum instead of squeezing the upper back.
cue_isometric_wipers_1: Assume a push-up position, supporting your weight on your hands and toes while keeping your body straight. Your hands should be just outside of shoulder width.
cue_isometric_wipers_2: Begin by shifting your body weight as far to one side as possible, allowing the elbow on that side to flex as you lower your body.
cue_isometric_wipers_mistake: Flaring elbows too wide or bouncing at the bottom.
cue_it_band_and_glute_stretch_1: Loop a belt, rope, or band around one of your feet, and swing that leg across your body to the opposite side, keeping the leg extended as you lay on the ground.
cue_it_band_and_glute_stretch_2: Keeping your foot off of the floor, pull on the belt, using the tension to pull the toes up. Hold for 10-20 seconds, and repeat on the other side.
cue_it_band_and_glute_stretch_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_jackknife_sit_up_1: Start long on the floor with arms overhead.
cue_jackknife_sit_up_2: Lift torso and straight legs together to meet in the middle.
cue_jackknife_sit_up_mistake: Bending knees sharply or slamming back down.
cue_janda_sit_up_1: Position your body on the floor in the basic sit-up position; knees to a ninety degree angle with feet flat on the floor and arms either crossed over your chest or to the sides.
cue_janda_sit_up_2: As you strongly tighten your glutes and hamstrings, fill your lungs with air and in a slow (three to six second count) ascent, slowly exhale.
cue_janda_sit_up_mistake: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_jefferson_squats_1: Place a barbell on the floor.
cue_jefferson_squats_2: Stand in the middle of the bar length wise.
cue_jefferson_squats_mistake: Letting knees cave inward or heels lift off the floor.
cue_jm_press_1: Use a shoulder-width grip and let elbows drift slightly forward.
cue_jm_press_2: Lower the bar toward your chin/upper chest, then drive up.
cue_jm_press_mistake: Dropping elbows wide like a flat bench press.
cue_jogging_treadmill_1: To begin, step onto the treadmill and select the desired option from the menu. Most treadmills have a manual setting, or you can select a program to run.
cue_jogging_treadmill_2: Treadmills offer convenience, cardiovascular benefits, and usually have less impact than jogging outside.
cue_jogging_treadmill_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.
cue_jump_rope_1: Turn the rope from your wrists, elbows tucked at sides.
cue_jump_rope_2: Stay light on the balls of your feet with tiny bounces.
cue_jump_rope_mistake: Swinging the whole arms or jumping too high.
cue_jump_squat_1: Quarter-to-half squat smoothly, then explode straight up.
cue_jump_squat_2: Land softly on mid-foot absorbing the drop into the next rep.
cue_jumping_jacks_1: Land softly on the balls of your feet.
cue_jumping_jacks_2: Keep your arms moving in a full, easy arc.
cue_jumping_jacks_mistake: Stomping down hard and locking the knees.
cue_kb_alternating_press_1: Clean both bells to rack position with tight glutes and abs.
cue_kb_alternating_press_2: Press one overhead while keeping the other anchored.
cue_kb_alternating_press_mistake: Leaning back to push the weight.
cue_kb_alternating_row_1: Hinge with a neutral back and brace your core.
cue_kb_alternating_row_2: Row one bell toward your hip while lowering the other.
cue_kb_alternating_row_mistake: Rounding the spine or jerking upward.
cue_kb_arnold_press_1: Start in the rack position with palm facing inward.
cue_kb_arnold_press_2: Rotate wrist outward as you press the bell overhead.
cue_kb_arnold_press_mistake: Arching the lower back during lockout.
cue_kb_clean_1: Hinge back, then pull the bell close and into the rack.
cue_kb_clean_2: Keep the bell close to the body.
cue_kb_clean_mistake: Letting the bell swing out and bang the forearm.
cue_kb_deadlift_1: Hinge back with a flat spine and the bell between your feet.
cue_kb_deadlift_2: Stand tall by driving the hips forward.
cue_kb_deadlift_mistake: Rounding the back to reach the bell.
cue_kb_double_front_squat_1: Rest bells in the front rack with elbows tucked forward.
cue_kb_double_front_squat_2: Sit deep between your heels keeping chest tall.
cue_kb_double_front_squat_mistake: Letting elbows drop forward and rounding upper back.
cue_kb_figure_8_1: Hold a quarter-squat hinge with flat back and tight core.
cue_kb_figure_8_2: Pass the bell smoothly between legs from hand to hand.
cue_kb_figure_8_mistake: Rounding the lower back while reaching down.
cue_kb_floor_press_1: Keep wrist straight and elbow tucked at 45 degrees.
cue_kb_floor_press_2: Pause with triceps on the floor, then press straight up.
cue_kb_floor_press_mistake: Flaring the elbow out to 90 degrees.
cue_kb_halo_1: Circle the bell close to the head with the ribs down.
cue_kb_halo_2: Keep the elbows tucked and move slowly.
cue_kb_halo_mistake: Leaning back as the bell passes behind the head.
cue_kb_one_arm_swing_1: Hinge at the hips and keep shoulders square—no twisting.
cue_kb_one_arm_swing_2: Snap hips forward to float the bell to chest height.
cue_kb_one_arm_swing_mistake: Squatting down or lifting with the front shoulder.
cue_kb_pistol_squat_1: Hold the kettlebell out front or racked as a counterbalance.
cue_kb_pistol_squat_2: Sit smoothly onto the working heel and drive straight up.
cue_kb_pistol_squat_mistake: Collapsing the knee inward at the bottom.
cue_kb_press_1: Brace the core and press the bell straight overhead.
cue_kb_press_2: Finish with the biceps by the ear and the ribs down.
cue_kb_press_mistake: Leaning back to push the bell up.
cue_kb_renegade_row_1: Set feet wider than shoulder width in a strong plank.
cue_kb_renegade_row_2: Row one bell to your hip while keeping hips square to floor.
cue_kb_renegade_row_mistake: Rotating or hiking one hip upward with each row.
cue_kb_row_1: Hinge forward with a flat back and row the bell to the hip.
cue_kb_row_2: Squeeze the shoulder blade back at the top.
cue_kb_row_mistake: Twisting the torso to lift the bell.
cue_kb_seated_press_1: Sit tall with core braced and wrist straight.
cue_kb_seated_press_2: Press straight overhead until bicep aligns by your ear.
cue_kb_seated_press_mistake: Letting the kettlebell pull your wrist backward.
cue_kb_snatch_1: Swing from the hips and punch the bell overhead.
cue_kb_snatch_2: Keep the arm close and lock out the elbow.
cue_kb_snatch_mistake: Pulling with the arm and hitting the wrist.
cue_kb_sumo_deadlift_1: Take a wide stance with the toes out and the back flat.
cue_kb_sumo_deadlift_2: Drive the floor away and stand tall.
cue_kb_sumo_deadlift_mistake: Rounding the back or letting the knees cave in.
cue_kb_sumo_high_pull_1: Stand wide, hinge down with flat back, and drive hips up.
cue_kb_sumo_high_pull_2: Pull elbows high to chin height as hips finish locking.
cue_kb_sumo_high_pull_mistake: Pulling only with the arms before hips extend.
cue_kb_swing_1: Hinge the hips back and snap them forward.
cue_kb_swing_2: Let the arms swing; the hips drive the bell.
cue_kb_swing_mistake: Squatting the swing or lifting with the arms.
cue_kb_thruster_1: Hold the bell in rack position and squat to parallel.
cue_kb_thruster_2: Drive smoothly out of the squat directly into an overhead press.
cue_kb_thruster_mistake: Pausing at the top of the squat before pressing.
cue_kb_windmill_1: Keep your eyes on the bell and hinge toward the front leg.
cue_kb_windmill_2: Slide the hand down the leg while the arm stays straight.
cue_kb_windmill_mistake: Bending the arm or rushing the hinge.
cue_kettlebell_dead_clean_1: Place kettlebell between your feet. To get in the starting position, push your butt back and look straight ahead.
cue_kettlebell_dead_clean_2: Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder.
cue_kettlebell_dead_clean_mistake: Rounding the lower back under load.
cue_kettlebell_halo_1: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart. Hold a kettlebell upside down by the horns, with the bell above your hands and close to your chest.
cue_kettlebell_halo_2: Keeping your elbows close to your head, move the kettlebell up past one ear and around behind your head.
cue_kettlebell_halo_mistake: Arching the lower back excessively instead of bracing.
cue_kettlebell_halo_with_overhead_extens: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart. Hold a kettlebell upside down by the horns, with the bell above your hands and close to your chest.
Keeping your elbows close to your head, move the kettlebell up past one ear and around until it sits behind your head. Pause here.
Arching the lower back excessively instead of bracing.
cue_kettlebell_hang_clean_1: Place kettlebell between your feet. To get in the starting position, push your butt back and look straight ahead.
cue_kettlebell_hang_clean_mistake: Rounding the lower back under load.
cue_kettlebell_overhead_triceps_extensio: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a kettlebell by the horns with both hands.
Brace your abdominals and keep your upper arms vertical and close to your head. This is your starting position.
Letting elbows flare or drift during the press.
cue_kettlebell_pass_between_the_legs_1: Place one kettlebell between your legs and take a comfortable stance. Bend over by pushing your butt out and keeping your back flat.
cue_kettlebell_pass_between_the_legs_2: Pick up a kettlebell and pass it to your other hand between your legs, in the fashion of a "W". Go back and forth for several repetitions.
cue_kettlebell_pass_between_the_legs_mis: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_kettlebell_pirate_ships_1: With a wide stance, hold a kettlebell with both hands. Allow it to hang at waist level with your arms extended. This will be your starting position.
cue_kettlebell_pirate_ships_2: Initiate the movement by turning to one side, swinging the kettlebell to head height. Briefly pause at the top of the motion.
cue_kettlebell_pirate_ships_mistake: Arching the lower back excessively instead of bracing.
cue_kettlebell_seesaw_press_1: Clean two kettlebells two your shoulders.
cue_kettlebell_seesaw_press_mistake: Arching the lower back excessively instead of bracing.
cue_kettlebell_turkish_get_up_lunge_styl: Lie on your back on the floor and press a kettlebell to the top position by extending the elbow. Bend the knee on the same side as the kettlebell.
Keeping the kettlebell locked out at all times, pivot to the opposite side and use your non- working arm to assist you in driving forward to the lunge position.
Letting the front knee collapse inward.
cue_kipping_muscle_up_1: Grip the rings using a false grip, with the base of your palms on top of the rings.
cue_kipping_muscle_up_2: Begin with a movement swinging your legs backward slightly.
cue_kipping_muscle_up_mistake: Rounding the upper back or jerking the weight.
cue_knee_across_the_body_1: Lie down on the floor with your right leg straight.
cue_knee_across_the_body_2: Place your left arm comfortably beside you and turn your head to the left. Imagine you have a weight tied to your tailbone.
cue_knee_across_the_body_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_knee_circles_1: Stand with your legs together and hands by your waist.
cue_knee_circles_2: Now move your knees in a circular motion as you breathe normally.
cue_knee_circles_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_knee_push_up_1: Keep a straight line from the knees to the head.
cue_knee_push_up_2: Lower the chest toward the floor, elbows at about 45 degrees.
cue_knee_push_up_mistake: Sagging the hips or flaring the elbows wide.
cue_knee_scapular_push_up_1: Keep the arms straight and move only the shoulder blades.
cue_knee_scapular_push_up_2: Push the floor away to spread them, then squeeze them back.
cue_knee_scapular_push_up_mistake: Bending the elbows instead of moving the shoulders.
cue_knee_tuck_jump_1: Begin in a comfortable standing position with your knees slightly bent.
cue_knee_tuck_jump_2: Rapidly dip down into a quarter squat and immediately explode upward. Drive the knees towards the chest, attempting to touch them to the palms of the hands.
cue_knee_tuck_jump_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.
cue_kneeling_arm_drill_1: This drill helps increase arm efficiency during the run. Begin kneeling, left foot in front, right knee down.
cue_kneeling_arm_drill_2: Begin by blocking the arms in long, pendulum like swings.
cue_kneeling_arm_drill_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.
cue_kneeling_cable_crunch_with_alternati: Connect a rope attachment to a high pulley cable and position a mat on the floor in front of it.
Grab the rope with both hands and kneel approximately two feet back from the tower.
Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_kneeling_cable_triceps_extension_1: Place a bench sideways in front of a high pulley machine.
cue_kneeling_cable_triceps_extension_2: Hold a straight bar attachment above your head with your hands about 6 inches apart with your palms facing down.
cue_kneeling_cable_triceps_extension_mis: Letting elbows flare or drift during the press.
cue_kneeling_high_pulley_row_1: Brace abs while kneeling and let lats stretch overhead.
cue_kneeling_high_pulley_row_2: Pull handles toward your upper ribs, elbows tight.
cue_kneeling_squat_1: Set the bar to the proper height in a power rack. Kneel behind the bar; it may be beneficial to put a mat down to pad your knees.
cue_kneeling_squat_2: With your head looking forward, sit back with your butt until you touch your calves.
cue_kneeling_squat_mistake: Letting knees cave inward or heels lift off the floor.
cue_l_sit_1: Press the shoulders down and lock the arms.
cue_l_sit_2: Keep the legs straight and squeezed together.
cue_l_sit_mistake: Shrugging the shoulders and bending the knees.
cue_l_sit_pull_up_1: Hang and lift the straight legs to hip height.
cue_l_sit_pull_up_2: Hold the legs there while you pull the chin over the bar.
cue_l_sit_pull_up_mistake: Letting the legs drop as you pull.
cue_landmine_linear_jammer_1: Position a bar into landmine or, lacking one, securely anchor it in a corner.
cue_landmine_linear_jammer_2: Raise the bar from the floor, taking the handles to your shoulders. This will be your starting position.
cue_landmine_linear_jammer_mistake: Arching the lower back excessively instead of bracing.
cue_landmine_one_arm_row_1: Stagger your stance and rest your free hand on your thigh.
cue_landmine_one_arm_row_2: Drive the elbow back toward your hip without twisting.
cue_landmine_one_arm_row_mistake: Rounding the lower back or rotating the torso.
cue_landmine_press_1: Brace your core and lean slightly into the bar angle.
cue_landmine_press_2: Press up and forward along the natural arc.
cue_landmine_press_mistake: Twisting the torso or shrugging the shoulder.
cue_landmine_twist_1: Keep arms nearly straight and brace abs with soft knees.
cue_landmine_twist_2: Rotate the bar in an arc from hip to hip using your core.
cue_landmine_twist_mistake: Swinging from the arms while the hips flop side to side.
cue_lat_pulldown_1: Pull the bar to the upper chest, elbows toward the floor.
cue_lat_pulldown_2: Sit tall and keep the shoulders down.
cue_lat_pulldown_mistake: Leaning far back and yanking the bar down.
cue_lat_stretch_1: Reach one arm overhead and lean to the opposite side.
cue_lat_stretch_2: Keep both feet planted and the hips level.
cue_lateral_bound_1: Assume a half squat position facing 90 degrees from your direction of travel. This will be your starting position.
cue_lateral_bound_2: Allow your lead leg to do a countermovement inward as you shift your weight to the outside leg.
cue_lateral_bound_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.
cue_lateral_box_jump_1: Assume a comfortable standing position, with a short box positioned next to you. This will be your starting position.
cue_lateral_box_jump_2: Quickly dip into a quarter squat to initiate the stretch reflex, and immediately reverse direction to jump up and to the side.
cue_lateral_box_jump_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.
cue_lateral_cone_hops_1: Position a number of cones in a row several feet apart.
cue_lateral_cone_hops_2: Stand next to the end of the cones, facing 90 degrees to the direction of travel. This will be your starting position.
cue_lateral_cone_hops_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.
cue_lateral_raise_1: Lead with the elbows and lift to shoulder height.
cue_lateral_raise_2: Use light weights and lower slowly.
cue_lateral_raise_mistake: Swinging the weights with the torso.
cue_latissimus_dorsi_smr_1: While lying on the floor, place a foam roll under your back and to one side, just behind your arm pit. This will be your starting position.
cue_latissimus_dorsi_smr_2: Keep the arm of the side being stretched behind and to the side of you as you shift your weight onto your lats, keeping your upper body off of the ground.
cue_latissimus_dorsi_smr_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_leg_curl_1: Keep the hips pressed down and curl the heels toward the glutes.
cue_leg_curl_2: Lower slowly through the full range.
cue_leg_curl_mistake: Lifting the hips off the pad.
cue_leg_extension_1: Set the pad above the ankles and extend smoothly.
cue_leg_extension_2: Squeeze the quads at the top and lower slowly.
cue_leg_extension_mistake: Swinging the weight up with momentum.
cue_leg_lift_1: While standing up straight with both feet next to each other at around shoulder width, grab a sturdy surface such as the sides of a squat rack or the top of a chair to brace yourself and keep balance.
cue_leg_lift_2: With or without an ankle weight, lift one leg behind you as if performing a leg curl but standing up while keeping the other leg straight.
cue_leg_lift_mistake: Rounding the lower back under load.
cue_leg_over_floor_press_1: Lie on the floor with one kettlebell in place on your chest, holding it by the handle. Extend leg on working side over leg on non-working side.
cue_leg_over_floor_press_2: Press the kettlebll into a locked out position.
cue_leg_over_floor_press_mistake: Flaring elbows too wide or bouncing at the bottom.
cue_leg_press_1: Keep the lower back and hips pressed into the seat.
cue_leg_press_2: Lower until the knees reach a deep angle, then press.
cue_leg_press_calf_raise_1: Place balls of your feet near the bottom edge of the sled.
cue_leg_press_calf_raise_2: Keep knees softly unlocked and press through full ankle range.
cue_leg_press_calf_raise_mistake: Bouncing fast without pausing at stretch and peak.
cue_leg_press_mistake: Letting the hips curl off the seat at the bottom.
cue_leg_pull_in_1: Lie on an exercise mat with your legs extended and your hands either palms facing down next to you or under your glutes.
cue_leg_pull_in_2: Bend your knees and pull your upper thighs into your midsection as you breathe out. Continue the motion until your knees are around chest level.
cue_leg_pull_in_mistake: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_leg_up_hamstring_stretch_1: Lie flat on your back, bend one knee, and put that foot flat on the floor to stabilize your spine.
cue_leg_up_hamstring_stretch_2: Extend the other leg in the air. If you're tight, you wont be able to straighten it. That's okay.
cue_leg_up_hamstring_stretch_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_leverage_chest_press_1: Load an appropriate weight onto the pins and adjust the seat for your height.
cue_leverage_chest_press_2: Your chest and head should be up and your shoulder blades retracted. This will be your starting position.
cue_leverage_chest_press_mistake: Flaring elbows too wide or bouncing at the bottom.
cue_leverage_deadlift_1: Load the pins to an appropriate weight. Position yourself directly between the handles.
cue_leverage_deadlift_2: Return the weight to the starting position.
cue_leverage_deadlift_mistake: Rounding the lower back under load.
cue_leverage_shoulder_press_1: Set seat height so handles begin at chin level.
cue_leverage_shoulder_press_2: Keep back pressed into the pad and push evenly.
cue_leverage_shoulder_press_mistake: Shrugging traps at the top or bouncing off stops.
cue_leverage_shrug_1: Load the pins to an appropriate weight. Position yourself directly between the handles.
cue_leverage_shrug_2: Grasp the top handles with a comfortable grip, and then lower your hips as you take a breath. Look forward with your head and keep your chest up.
cue_leverage_shrug_mistake: Using heavy momentum instead of squeezing the upper back.
cue_linear_3_part_start_technique_1: This drill helps you accelerate as quickly as possible into a sprint from a dead stop. It helps to use a line to start from. Begin with two feet on the line.
cue_linear_3_part_start_technique_2: Place your right hand onto the line, and thing bring your nose close to your left knee.
cue_linear_3_part_start_technique_mistak: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.
cue_linear_acceleration_wall_drill_1: Lean at around 45 degrees against a wall. Your feet should be together, glutes contracted.
cue_linear_acceleration_wall_drill_2: Begin by lifting your right knee quickly, pausing, and then driving it straight down into the ground.
cue_linear_acceleration_wall_drill_mista: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.
cue_linear_depth_jump_1: You will need two boxes or benches spaced a few feet away from each other. Begin by standing on one box facing towards the other platform.
cue_linear_depth_jump_2: To initiate the movement, gently drop down to the ground between your platforms, allowing the knees and hips to flex.
cue_linear_depth_jump_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.
cue_london_bridges_1: Attach a climbing rope to a high beam or cross member. Below it, ensure that the smith machine bar is locked in place with the safeties and cannot move.
cue_london_bridges_2: Stand on the bar, using the rope to balance yourself. This will be your starting position.
cue_london_bridges_mistake: Letting the lower back sag toward the floor.
cue_looking_at_ceiling_1: Kneel on the floor, holding your heels with both hands.
cue_looking_at_ceiling_2: Lift your buttocks up and forward while bringing your head back to look up at the ceiling, to give an arch in your back.
cue_looking_at_ceiling_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_low_cable_tricep_ext_1: Face away from the low pulley with a staggered stance.
cue_low_cable_tricep_ext_2: Keep elbows close to your head and press forward-up.
cue_low_cable_tricep_ext_mistake: Arching the lower back under heavy load.
cue_low_pulley_row_to_neck_1: Sit on a low pulley row machine with a rope attachment.
cue_low_pulley_row_to_neck_2: Grab the ends of the rope using a palms-down grip and sit with your back straight and your knees slightly bent.
cue_low_pulley_row_to_neck_mistake: Rounding the upper back or jerking the weight.
cue_lower_back_curl_1: Lie on your stomach with your arms out to your sides. This will be your starting position.
cue_lower_back_curl_2: Using your lower back muscles, extend your spine lifting your chest off of the ground. Do not use your arms to push yourself up.
cue_lower_back_curl_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_lower_back_smr_1: In a seated position, place a foam roll under your lower back. Cross your arms in front of you and protract your shoulders. This will be your starting position.
cue_lower_back_smr_2: Raise your hips off of the floor and lean back, keeping your weight on your lower back.
cue_lower_back_smr_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_lunge_1: Take a long step and drop the back knee straight down.
cue_lunge_2: Keep the torso upright and the front foot flat.
cue_lunge_mistake: Letting the front knee collapse inward.
cue_lunge_pass_through_1: Stand with your torso upright holding a kettlebell in your right hand. This will be your starting position.
cue_lunge_pass_through_2: Step forward with your left foot and lower your upper body down by flexing the hip and the knee, keeping the torso upright.
cue_lunge_pass_through_mistake: Letting the front knee collapse inward.
cue_lunge_sprint_1: Adjust a bar in a Smith machine to an appropriate height. Position yourself under the bar, racking it across the back of your shoulders.
cue_lunge_sprint_2: Lower your back knee nearly to the ground, flexing the knees and lowering your hips as you do so.
cue_lunge_sprint_mistake: Letting the front knee collapse inward.
cue_lying_bent_leg_groin_1: Lie on your back with your knees bent and the soles of the feet pressed together. Have your partner hold your knees. This will be your starting position.
cue_lying_bent_leg_groin_2: Attempt to squeeze your knees together, while your partner prevents any movement from occurring.
cue_lying_bent_leg_groin_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_lying_cable_curl_1: Grab a straight bar or E-Z bar attachment that is attached to the low pulley with both hands, using an underhand (palms facing up) shoulder-width grip.
cue_lying_cable_curl_2: Lie flat on your back on top of an exercise mat in front of the weight stack with your feet flat against the frame of the pulley machine and your legs straight.
cue_lying_cable_curl_mistake: Swinging the elbows forward to heave the weight.
cue_lying_close_grip_bar_curl_on_high_pu: Place a flat bench in front of a high pulley or lat pulldown machine.
Hold the straight bar attachment using an underhand grip (palms up) that is about shoulder width.
Swinging the elbows forward to heave the weight.
cue_lying_close_grip_barbell_triceps_pre: While holding a barbell or EZ Curl bar with a pronated grip (palms facing forward), lie on your back on a flat bench with your head off the end of the bench.
Extend your arms in front of you as you hold the barbell over your chest. The arms should be perpendicular to your torso (90-degree angle).
Swinging the elbows forward to heave the weight.
cue_lying_crossover_1: Lie on your back with your legs extended.
cue_lying_crossover_2: Cross one leg over your body with the knee bent, attempting to touch the knee to the ground.
cue_lying_crossover_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_lying_dumbbell_tricep_extension_1: Lie on a flat bench while holding two dumbbells directly in front of you. Your arms should be fully extended at a 90-degree angle from your torso and the floor.
cue_lying_dumbbell_tricep_extension_2: As you breathe in and you keep the upper arms stationary with the elbows in, slowly lower the weight until the dumbbells are near your ears.
cue_lying_dumbbell_tricep_extension_mist: Letting elbows flare or drift during the press.
cue_lying_face_down_plate_neck_resistanc: Lie face down with your whole body straight on a flat bench while holding a weight plate behind your head.
While keeping the plate secure on the back of your head slowly lower your head (as in saying "yes") as you breathe in.
Using heavy momentum instead of squeezing the upper back.
cue_lying_face_up_plate_neck_resistance_: Lie face up with your whole body straight on a flat bench while holding a weight plate on top of your forehead.
While keeping the plate secure on your forehead slowly lower your head back in a semi-circular motion as you breathe in.
Using heavy momentum instead of squeezing the upper back.
cue_lying_glute_1: Lie on your back with your partner kneeling beside you.
cue_lying_glute_2: Flex the hip of one leg, raising it off of the floor. Rotate the leg so the foot is over the opposite hip, the lower leg perpendicular to your body.
cue_lying_glute_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_lying_hamstring_1: Lie on your back with your legs extended. Your partner should be kneeling beside you. Raise one leg up towards the ceiling and have your partner hold the ankle.
cue_lying_hamstring_2: With your partner holding your leg in place, attempt to flex the knee, contracting the hamstrings for 10-20 seconds.
cue_lying_hamstring_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_lying_high_bench_barbell_curl_1: Lie face forward on a tall flat bench while holding a barbell with a supinated grip (palms facing up).
cue_lying_high_bench_barbell_curl_2: While keeping the elbows in and the upper arms stationary, curl the weight up in a semi-circular motion as you contract the biceps and exhale.
cue_lying_high_bench_barbell_curl_mistak: Swinging the elbows forward to heave the weight.
cue_lying_leg_raise_1: Grip the bench behind your head and press lower back flat.
cue_lying_leg_raise_2: Raise straight legs to vertical and lower slowly without arching.
cue_lying_leg_raise_mistake: Letting legs drop below bench level with an arched back.
cue_lying_machine_squat_1: Adjust the leg machine to a height that will allow you to get inside it with your knees bent and the thighs slightly below parallel.
cue_lying_machine_squat_2: Once you select the weight, position yourself inside the machine face up with the knees bent and thighs slightly below parallel to the platform.
cue_lying_machine_squat_mistake: Letting knees cave inward or heels lift off the floor.
cue_lying_one_arm_lateral_raise_1: While holding a dumbbell in one hand, lay with your chest down on a flat bench. The other hand can be used to hold to the leg of the bench for stability.
cue_lying_one_arm_lateral_raise_2: Position the palm of the hand that is holding the dumbbell in a neutral manner (palms facing your torso) as you keep the arm extended with the elbow slightly bent.
cue_lying_one_arm_lateral_raise_mistake: Swinging the torso to lift with momentum.
cue_lying_prone_quadriceps_1: Lay face down on the floor with your partner kneeling beside you.
cue_lying_prone_quadriceps_2: Attempt to extend your knee while your partner prevents any actual movement.
cue_lying_prone_quadriceps_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_lying_rear_delt_raise_1: While holding a dumbbell in each hand, lay with your chest down on a flat bench.
cue_lying_rear_delt_raise_2: Position the palms of the hands in a neutral manner (palms facing your torso) as you keep the arms extended with the elbows slightly bent.
cue_lying_rear_delt_raise_mistake: Using heavy momentum instead of squeezing the upper back.
cue_lying_supine_dumbbell_curl_1: Lie down on a flat bench face up while holding a dumbbell in each arm on top of your thighs.
cue_lying_supine_dumbbell_curl_2: Bring the dumbbells to the sides with the arms extended and the palms of the hands facing your thighs (neutral grip).
cue_lying_supine_dumbbell_curl_mistake: Swinging the elbows forward to heave the weight.
cue_lying_t_bar_row_1: Keep your chest planted on the pad throughout.
cue_lying_t_bar_row_2: Pull elbows back and squeeze the mid-back.
cue_lying_t_bar_row_mistake: Lifting your chest off the pad to finish the pull.
cue_lying_triceps_press_1: Lie on a flat bench with either an e-z bar (my preference) or a straight bar placed on the floor behind your head and your feet on the floor.
cue_lying_triceps_press_2: Grab the bar behind you, using a medium overhand (pronated) grip, and raise the bar in front of you at arms length.
cue_lying_triceps_press_mistake: Letting elbows flare or drift during the press.
cue_medicine_ball_chest_pass_1: You will need a partner for this exercise. Lacking one, this movement can be performed against a wall.
cue_medicine_ball_chest_pass_2: Begin facing your partner holding the medicine ball at your torso with both hands.
cue_medicine_ball_chest_pass_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.
cue_medicine_ball_full_twist_1: For this exercise you will need a medicine ball and a partner. Stand back to back with your partner, spaced 2-3 feet apart. This will be your starting position.
cue_medicine_ball_full_twist_2: Hold the ball in front of the trunk. Open the hips and turn the shoulders at the same time as your partner.
cue_medicine_ball_full_twist_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.
cue_medicine_ball_scoop_throw_1: Assume a semisquat stance with a medicine ball in your hands. Your arms should hang so the ball is near your feet.
cue_medicine_ball_scoop_throw_2: Begin by thrusting the hips forward as you extend through the legs, jumping up.
cue_medicine_ball_scoop_throw_mistake: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_middle_back_shrug_1: Lie facedown on an incline bench while holding a dumbbell in each hand. Your arms should be fully extended hanging down and pointing towards the floor.
cue_middle_back_shrug_2: As you exhale, squeeze your shoulder blades together and hold the contraction for a full second.
cue_middle_back_shrug_mistake: Using heavy momentum instead of squeezing the upper back.
cue_middle_back_stretch_1: Stand so your feet are shoulder width apart and your hands are on your hips.
cue_middle_back_stretch_2: Twist at your waist until you feel a stretch. Hold for 10 to 15 seconds, then twist to the other side.
cue_middle_back_stretch_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_mixed_grip_chin_up_1: Place one palm facing you and one facing away; switch sets.
cue_mixed_grip_chin_up_2: Pull smoothly until chin clears the bar.
cue_monster_walk_1: Place a band around both ankles and another around both knees. There should be enough tension that they are tight when your feet are shoulder width apart.
cue_monster_walk_2: To begin, take short steps forward alternating your left and right foot.
cue_monster_walk_mistake: Rounding the lower back under load.
cue_mountain_climber_1: Keep the shoulders over the wrists and the core braced.
cue_mountain_climber_2: Drive the knees in with a steady rhythm.
cue_moving_claw_series_1: This move helps prepare your running form to help you excel at sprinting. As you run, be sure to flex the knee, aiming to kick your glutes as the hip extends.
cue_moving_claw_series_2: Reload the quad as the leg moves back forward, attacking the ground on the next step.
cue_moving_claw_series_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.
cue_muscle_up_1: Pull explosively and lean back over the bar.
cue_muscle_up_2: Lead with the chest and press out above the bar.
cue_muscle_up_mistake: Pulling with straight hips and arms too long.
cue_narrow_leg_press_1: Place feet lower and closer on the sled, heels planted.
cue_narrow_leg_press_2: Lower until knees reach full comfortable bend without lifting hips.
cue_narrow_leg_press_mistake: Locking knees violently or lifting lower back off the pad.
cue_narrow_stance_hack_squats_1: Place the back of your torso against the back pad of the machine and hook your shoulders under the shoulder pads provided.
cue_narrow_stance_hack_squats_2: Position your legs in the platform using a less than shoulder width narrow stance with the toes slightly pointed out.
cue_narrow_stance_hack_squats_mistake: Rounding the upper back or jerking the weight.
cue_narrow_stance_squat_1: Place feet hip-width or narrower and keep torso upright.
cue_narrow_stance_squat_2: Let knees track over toes and drive up through midfoot.
cue_narrow_stance_squat_mistake: Heels lifting off the floor at the bottom.
cue_neck_press_1: Lie back on a flat bench.
cue_neck_press_2: As you breathe in, come down slowly until you feel the bar on your neck.
cue_neck_press_mistake: Flaring elbows too wide or bouncing at the bottom.
cue_neck_side_stretch_1: Tilt your ear toward your shoulder and keep the shoulder down.
cue_neck_side_stretch_2: Let the weight of the head do the work.
cue_neck_side_stretch_mistake: Pulling the head hard with the hand.
cue_neck_smr_1: Using a muscle roller or a rolling pin, place the roller behind your head and against your neck.
cue_neck_smr_2: Starting at the top of your neck, slowly roll down the muscles of your neck, pausing at points of tension for 10-30 seconds.
cue_neck_smr_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_negative_pull_up_1: Jump to the top and lower for a slow count of five.
cue_negative_pull_up_2: Keep the body tight and the shoulders down.
cue_negative_pull_up_mistake: Dropping fast instead of controlling the descent.
cue_neutral_grip_db_press_1: Hold palms facing each other and tuck elbows at 30 degrees.
cue_neutral_grip_db_press_2: Lower deep beside the chest and press straight up.
cue_neutral_grip_db_press_mistake: Dropping shoulders forward at the top.
cue_neutral_grip_pull_up_1: Grip the parallel handles with the palms facing each other.
cue_neutral_grip_pull_up_2: Pull the elbows down to the ribs until the chin clears the handles.
cue_neutral_grip_pull_up_mistake: Cutting the bottom short instead of reaching straight arms.
cue_nordic_curl_1: Keep the hips extended and lower from the knees as one line.
cue_nordic_curl_2: Lower as slowly as you can, then push off to return.
cue_oblique_crunches_1: Lie flat on the floor with your lower back pressed to the ground.
cue_oblique_crunches_2: Make sure your feet are elevated and resting on a flat surface.
cue_oblique_crunches_mistake: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_oblique_crunches_on_the_floor_1: Start out by lying on your right side with your legs lying on top of each other. Make sure your knees are bent a little bit.
cue_oblique_crunches_on_the_floor_2: Place your left hand behind your head.
cue_oblique_crunches_on_the_floor_mistak: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_on_your_back_quad_stretch_1: Lie on a flat bench or step, and hang one leg and arm over the side.
cue_on_your_back_quad_stretch_2: Bend the knee and hold the top of the foot. As you do this, be careful not to arch your lower back.
cue_on_your_back_quad_stretch_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_on_your_side_quad_stretch_1: Start off by lying on your right side, with your right knee bent at a 90-degree angle resting on the floor in front of you (this stabilizes the torso).
cue_on_your_side_quad_stretch_2: Bend your left knee behind you and hold your left foot with your left hand.
cue_on_your_side_quad_stretch_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_one_arm_chin_up_1: For this exercise, start out by placing a towel around a chin up bar.
cue_one_arm_chin_up_2: Grab the chin-up bar with your palm facing you. One hand will be grabbing the chin-up bar and the other will be grabbing the towel.
cue_one_arm_chin_up_mistake: Pulling with momentum or stopping short of full range.
cue_one_arm_flat_bench_dumbbell_flye_1: Lie down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand resting on top of your thigh. The palm of your hand with the dumbbell in it should be at a neutral grip.
cue_one_arm_flat_bench_dumbbell_flye_2: By using your thighs to help you get the dumbbell up, clean the dumbbell so that you can hold it in front of you with your lifting arm being fully extended.
cue_one_arm_flat_bench_dumbbell_flye_mis: Flaring elbows too wide or bouncing at the bottom.
cue_one_arm_floor_press_1: Lie down on a flat surface with your back pressing against the floor or an exercise mat. Make sure your knees are bent.
cue_one_arm_floor_press_2: Have a partner hand you the bar on one hand.
cue_one_arm_floor_press_mistake: Flaring elbows too wide or bouncing at the bottom.
cue_one_arm_incline_lateral_raise_1: Lie down sideways on an incline bench press with a dumbbell in the hand.
cue_one_arm_incline_lateral_raise_2: Hold a dumbbell in your uppermost arm while keeping it extended in front of you parallel to the floor. This is your starting position.
cue_one_arm_incline_lateral_raise_mistak: Swinging the torso to lift with momentum.
cue_one_arm_kettlebell_clean_and_jerk_1: Hold a kettlebell by the handle.
cue_one_arm_kettlebell_clean_and_jerk_2: Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulder.
cue_one_arm_kettlebell_clean_and_jerk_mi: Arching the lower back excessively instead of bracing.
cue_one_arm_kettlebell_para_press_1: Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder.
cue_one_arm_kettlebell_para_press_2: Hold the kettlebell with the elbow out to the side, and press it up and out until it is locked out overhead.
cue_one_arm_kettlebell_para_press_mistak: Arching the lower back excessively instead of bracing.
cue_one_arm_kettlebell_push_press_1: Hold a kettlebell by the handle. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulder.
cue_one_arm_kettlebell_push_press_2: Dip your body by bending the knees, keeping your torso upright.
cue_one_arm_kettlebell_push_press_mistak: Arching the lower back excessively instead of bracing.
cue_one_arm_kettlebell_split_jerk_1: Hold a kettlebell by the handle. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulder.
cue_one_arm_kettlebell_split_jerk_2: Dip your body by bending the knees, keeping your torso upright.
cue_one_arm_kettlebell_split_jerk_mistak: Arching the lower back excessively instead of bracing.
cue_one_arm_kettlebell_split_snatch_1: Hold a kettlebell in one hand by the handle.
cue_one_arm_kettlebell_split_snatch_2: Squat towards the floor, and then reverse the motion, extending the hips, knees, and finally the ankles, to raise the kettlebell overhead.
cue_one_arm_kettlebell_split_snatch_mist: Rounding the lower back under load.
cue_one_arm_long_bar_row_1: Position a bar into a landmine or in a corner to keep it from moving. Load an appropriate weight onto your end.
cue_one_arm_long_bar_row_2: Stand next to the bar, and take a grip with one hand close to the collar. Using your hips and legs, rise to a standing position.
cue_one_arm_long_bar_row_mistake: Rounding the upper back or jerking the weight.
cue_one_arm_medicine_ball_slam_1: Start in a standing position with a staggered, athletic stance. Hold a medicine ball in one hand, on the same side as your back leg.
cue_one_arm_medicine_ball_slam_2: Begin by winding the arm, raising the medicine ball above your head. As you do so, extend through the hips, knees, and ankles to load up for the slam.
cue_one_arm_medicine_ball_slam_mistake: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_one_arm_overhead_kettlebell_squats_1: Clean and press a kettlebell with one arm.
cue_one_arm_overhead_kettlebell_squats_2: Looking straight ahead and keeping a kettlebell locked out above you, flex the knees and hips and lower your torso between your legs, keeping your head and chest up.
cue_one_arm_overhead_kettlebell_squats_m: Letting knees cave inward or heels lift off the floor.
cue_one_arm_side_deadlift_1: Stand to the side of a barbell next to its center. Bend your knees and lower your body until you are able to reach the barbell.
cue_one_arm_side_deadlift_2: Grasp the bar as if you were grabbing a briefcase (palms facing you since the bar is sideways).
cue_one_arm_side_deadlift_mistake: Rounding the lower back under load.
cue_one_half_locust_2: Put your left hand under your left hipbone to pad your hip and pubic bone.
cue_one_half_locust_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_one_handed_hang_1: Grab onto a chinup bar with one hand, using a pronated grip. Keep your feet on the floor or a step.
cue_one_handed_hang_2: Move through a controlled full range of motion.
cue_one_handed_hang_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_one_knee_to_chest_1: Start off by lying on the floor.
cue_one_knee_to_chest_2: Extend one leg straight and pull the other knee to your chest. Hold under the knee joint to protect the kneecap.
cue_one_knee_to_chest_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_one_leg_barbell_squat_1: Start by standing about 2 to 3 feet in front of a flat bench with your back facing the bench. Have a barbell in front of you on the floor.
cue_one_leg_barbell_squat_2: Bend the knees and use a pronated grip with your hands being wider than shoulder width apart from each other to lift the barbell up until you can rest it on your chest.
cue_one_leg_barbell_squat_mistake: Letting knees cave inward or heels lift off the floor.
cue_open_palm_kettlebell_clean_1: Place one kettlebell between your feet. Clean the kettlebell by extending through the legs and hips as you raise the kettlebell towards your shoulders.
cue_open_palm_kettlebell_clean_2: Release the kettlebell as it comes up, and let it flip so that the ball of the kettlebell lands in the palms of your hands.
cue_open_palm_kettlebell_clean_mistake: Rounding the lower back under load.
cue_otis_up_1: Secure your feet and lay back on the floor. Your knees should be bent. Hold a weight with both hands to your chest. This will be your starting position.
cue_otis_up_2: Initiate the movement by flexing the hips and spine to raise your torso up from the ground.
cue_otis_up_mistake: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_overhead_cable_curl_1: To begin, set a weight that is comfortable on each side of the pulley machine. Note: Make sure that the amount of weight selected is the same on each side.
cue_overhead_cable_curl_2: Now adjust the height of the pulleys on each side and make sure that they are positioned at a height higher than that of your shoulders.
cue_overhead_cable_curl_mistake: Swinging the elbows forward to heave the weight.
cue_overhead_cable_triceps_extension_1: Keep the elbows high and pointed forward.
cue_overhead_cable_triceps_extension_2: Straighten the arms fully and return slowly.
cue_overhead_cable_triceps_extension_mis: Letting the elbows flare out wide.
cue_overhead_db_tricep_ext_1: Cup the top plate of one dumbbell overhead, elbows tucked.
cue_overhead_db_tricep_ext_2: Lower slowly behind your head and press straight up.
cue_overhead_db_tricep_ext_mistake: Letting elbows flare wide or arching the lower back.
cue_overhead_lat_1: Sit upright on the floor with your partner behind you. Raise one arm straight up, and flex the elbow, attempting to touch your hand to your back.
cue_overhead_lat_2: Attempt to pull your upper arm to your side as your partner prevents you from doing actually doing so.
cue_overhead_lat_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_overhead_press_1: Squeeze the glutes and keep the ribs down.
cue_overhead_press_2: Press the bar straight up, head moving through at the end.
cue_overhead_press_mistake: Leaning back to push the weight up.
cue_overhead_slam_1: Hold a medine ball with both hands and stand with your feet at shoulder width. This will be your starting position.
cue_overhead_slam_2: Initiate the countermovement by raising the ball above your head and fully extending your body.
cue_overhead_slam_mistake: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_overhead_squat_1: Lock the bar directly over mid-foot with active shoulders.
cue_overhead_squat_2: Sit straight down between your hips keeping the bar stacked.
cue_overhead_squat_mistake: Letting the bar drift forward of your toes.
cue_overhead_stretch_1: Standing straight up, lace your fingers together and open your palms to the ceiling. Keep your shoulders down as you extend your arms up.
cue_overhead_stretch_2: To create a full torso stretch, pull your tailbone down and stabilize your torso as you do this.
cue_overhead_stretch_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_overhead_triceps_1: Sit upright on the floor with your partner behind you. Raise one arm straight up, and flex the elbow, attempting to touch your hand to your back.
cue_overhead_triceps_2: Attempt to extend the arm straight into the air as your partner prevents you from doing actually doing so.
cue_overhead_triceps_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_pallof_press_1: Press the handle out and resist the cable pulling you.
cue_pallof_press_2: Keep the hips and shoulders square.
cue_pallof_press_mistake: Letting the torso rotate toward the cable.
cue_pallof_press_with_rotation_1: Connect a standard handle to a tower, and position the cable to shoulder height.
cue_pallof_press_with_rotation_2: With your side to the cable, grab the handle with one hand and step away from the tower.
cue_pallof_press_with_rotation_mistake: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_palms_down_dumbbell_wrist_curl_over_: Start out by placing two dumbbells on one side of a flat bench.
Kneel down on both of your knees so that your body is facing the flat bench.
Swinging the elbows forward to heave the weight.
cue_palms_up_barbell_wrist_curl_over_a_b: Start out by placing a barbell on one side of a flat bench.
Kneel down on both of your knees so that your body is facing the flat bench.
Swinging the elbows forward to heave the weight.
cue_palms_up_dumbbell_wrist_curl_over_a_: Start out by placing two dumbbells on one side of a flat bench.
Kneel down on both of your knees so that your body is facing the flat bench.
Swinging the elbows forward to heave the weight.
cue_pec_deck_1: Sit tall with the shoulder blades back against the pad.
cue_pec_deck_2: Bring the arms together and squeeze the chest.
cue_pec_deck_mistake: Rounding the shoulders forward at the end.
cue_pelvic_tilt_into_bridge_1: Lie down with your feet on the floor, heels directly under your knees.
cue_pelvic_tilt_into_bridge_2: Lift only your tailbone to the ceiling to stretch your lower back. (Don't lift the entire spine yet.) Pull in your stomach.
cue_pelvic_tilt_into_bridge_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_peroneals_smr_1: Lay on your side, supporting your weight on your forearm and on a foam roller placed on the outside of your lower leg.
cue_peroneals_smr_2: Raise your hips off of the ground and begin to roll from below the knee to above the ankle on the side of your leg, pausing at points of tension for 10-30 seconds.
cue_peroneals_smr_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_peroneals_stretch_1: In a seated position, loop a belt, rope, or band around one foot. This will be your starting position.
cue_peroneals_stretch_2: With the leg extended and the heel off of the ground, pull on the belt so that the foot is inverted, with the inside of the foot being pulled towards you.
cue_peroneals_stretch_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_physioball_hip_bridge_1: Lay on a ball so that your upper back is on the ball with your hips unsupported. Both feet should be flat on the floor, hip width apart or wider.
cue_physioball_hip_bridge_2: Begin by extending the hips using your glutes and hamstrings, raising your hips upward as you bridge.
cue_physioball_hip_bridge_mistake: Letting the lower back sag toward the floor.

cue_pigeon_stretch_2: Fold over the front leg and breathe out slowly.
cue_pigeon_stretch_mistake: Letting the hips twist off to one side.

cue_pike_push_up_2: Press back up until the arms are straight.

cue_piriformis_smr_1: Sit with your buttocks on top of a foam roll. Bend your knees, and then cross one leg so that the ankle is over the knee. This will be your starting position.

cue_piriformis_smr_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_pistol_squat_1: Reach the arms forward for balance and keep the heel down.
cue_pistol_squat_2: Lower under control with the free leg straight.

cue_plate_front_raise_1: Grip the sides of a weight plate like a steering wheel.

cue_plate_twist_mistake: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_platform_hamstring_slides_1: For this movement a wooden floor or similar is needed. Lay on your back with your legs extended. Place a gym towel or a light weight underneath your heel.
cue_platform_hamstring_slides_2: Begin the movement by flexing the knee, keeping your other leg straight.
cue_platform_hamstring_slides_mistake: Rounding the lower back under load.
cue_plyo_kettlebell_pushups_1: Place a kettlebell on the floor.

cue_plyo_kettlebell_pushups_mistake: Flaring elbows too wide or bouncing at the bottom.

cue_plyo_push_up_2: Land with soft elbows straight into the next rep.
cue_plyo_push_up_mistake: Landing stiff-armed or letting hips sag.
cue_posterior_tibialis_stretch_1: In a seated position, loop a belt, rope, or band around one foot. This will be your starting position.
cue_posterior_tibialis_stretch_2: With the leg extended and the heel off of the ground, pull on the belt so that the foot is everted, with the outside of the foot being pulled towards you.
cue_posterior_tibialis_stretch_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.

cue_power_clean_2: Whip elbows fast under the bar to catch on front shoulders.

cue_preacher_barbell_curl_1: Tuck armpits snugly over the top of the preacher pad.
cue_preacher_barbell_curl_2: Lower almost to full extension without snapping the elbow.

cue_preacher_hammer_curl_1: Hold dumbbells neutrally (palms facing each other) on the pad.
cue_preacher_hammer_curl_2: Lower slowly and stop just before full elbow lockout.
cue_preacher_hammer_curl_mistake: Bouncing out of the bottom position.
cue_press_sit_up_1: To begin, lie down on a bench with a barbell resting on your chest. Position your legs so they are secure on the extension of the abdominal bench.
cue_press_sit_up_2: While inhaling, tighten your abdominals and glutes.
cue_press_sit_up_mistake: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_prone_manual_hamstring_1: You will need a partner for this exercise. Lay face down with your legs straight. Your assistant will place their hand on your heel.

cue_prone_manual_hamstring_mistake: Rounding the lower back under load.
cue_prone_ytw_raise_1: Lie face down with your forehead resting and arms reaching overhead in a Y.
cue_prone_ytw_raise_2: Lift your arms off the floor by squeezing the shoulder blades, then move through the T and W shapes.
cue_prone_ytw_raise_mistake: Shrugging the shoulders toward your ears or arching the lower back.
cue_prowler_sprint_1: Place your sled on an appropriate surface, loaded to a suitable weight.
cue_prowler_sprint_2: You may use the upright or the low handles for this exercise. Place your hands on the handles with your arms extended, leaning into the implement.

cue_pseudo_planche_push_up_1: Place the hands by the hips with fingers pointing back.

cue_quick_leap_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.

cue_rear_leg_raises_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.

cue_recumbent_bike_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.
cue_return_push_from_stance_1: You will need a partner for this drill.

cue_reverse_band_power_squat_mistake: Letting knees cave inward or heels lift off the floor.

cue_reverse_hyperextension_mistake: Swinging the legs up using momentum.

cue_reverse_pec_deck_1: Lead with the elbows and open the arms wide.
cue_reverse_pec_deck_mistake: Shrugging and using the lower back to push.
cue_reverse_plate_curls_1: Start by standing straight with a weighted plate held by both hands and arms fully extended.

cue_reverse_plate_curls_mistake: Swinging the elbows forward to heave the weight.

cue_reverse_snow_angel_mistake: Bending the elbows or lifting the head too high.

cue_reverse_triceps_bench_press_mistake: Flaring elbows too wide or bouncing at the bottom.

cue_rocket_jump_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.

cue_round_the_world_shoulder_stretch_mis: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.

cue_runners_stretch_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.

cue_running_treadmill_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.

cue_scissor_kick_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.

cue_scissors_jump_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.

cue_seated_barbell_press_2: Press the bar overhead until biceps align by your ears.
cue_seated_barbell_press_mistake: Arching the lower back away from the bench.

cue_seated_barbell_twist_mistake: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.

cue_seated_biceps_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.

cue_seated_calf_stretch_2: Bend one knee and put that foot on the floor to stabilize the torso.
cue_seated_calf_stretch_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.

cue_upper_back_leg_grab_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_upper_back_stretch_1: Clasp fingers together with your thumbs pointing down, round your shoulders as you reach your hands forward.
cue_upper_back_stretch_2: Move through a controlled full range of motion.
cue_upper_back_stretch_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_upright_barbell_row_1: Take a shoulder-width grip to keep shoulders comfortable.
cue_upright_barbell_row_2: Lead with elbows up to chest height, bar close to body.
cue_upright_barbell_row_mistake: Pulling elbows higher than shoulders with a narrow grip.
cue_upright_cable_row_1: Stand tall with a straight bar on the low pulley.
cue_upright_cable_row_2: Drive elbows out and up to upper chest height.
cue_upright_cable_row_mistake: Curling the wrists inward at the top.
cue_upright_db_row_1: Pull dumbbells up along your torso, elbows leading.
cue_upright_db_row_2: Stop when upper arms reach parallel to the floor.
cue_upward_stretch_1: Extend both hands straight above your head, palms touching.
cue_upward_stretch_2: Slowly push your hands up and back, keeping your back straight.
cue_upward_stretch_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_v_bar_lat_pulldown_1: Use the V-handle with palms facing inward.
cue_v_bar_lat_pulldown_2: Pull elbows down toward your hips, chest proud.
cue_v_bar_lat_pulldown_mistake: Shrugging shoulders at the bottom of the rep.
cue_v_bar_pull_up_1: Pull chest toward the bar with elbows tight to your torso.
cue_v_bar_pull_up_2: Alternate which side of the bar your head clears each rep.
cue_v_bar_pull_up_mistake: Kipping or cutting the bottom stretch short.
cue_vertical_swing_1: Allow the dumbbell to hang at arms length between your legs, holding it with both hands. Keep your back straight and your head up.
cue_vertical_swing_2: Swing the dumbbell between your legs, flexing at the hips and bending the knees slightly.
cue_vertical_swing_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.
cue_walking_treadmill_1: To begin, step onto the treadmill and select the desired option from the menu. Most treadmills have a manual setting, or you can select a program to run.
cue_walking_treadmill_2: Treadmills offer convenience, cardiovascular benefits, and usually have less impact than walking outside.
cue_walking_treadmill_mistake: Losing posture or landing stiffly with locked knees.
cue_weighted_ball_hyperextension_1: To begin, lie down on an exercise ball with your torso pressing against the ball and parallel to the floor.
cue_weighted_ball_hyperextension_2: Slowly raise your torso up by bending at the waist and lower back. Remember to exhale during this movement.
cue_weighted_ball_hyperextension_mistake: Rounding the lower back under load.
cue_weighted_ball_side_bend_1: To begin, lie down on an exercise ball with your left side of the torso (waist, hips and shoulder) pressed against the ball.
cue_weighted_ball_side_bend_2: Your feet should be on the floor while your legs are crossed and hanging from the ball.
cue_weighted_ball_side_bend_mistake: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_weighted_bench_dip_1: Keep your back close to the bench and elbows pointing back.
cue_weighted_bench_dip_2: Lower until upper arms are parallel, then press up.
cue_weighted_bench_dip_mistake: Rolling shoulders forward at the bottom.
cue_weighted_chin_up_1: Pull from a full hang with palms facing you.
cue_weighted_chin_up_2: Lower slowly to a full hang each rep.
cue_weighted_chin_up_mistake: Using momentum with the extra weight.
cue_weighted_crunches_1: Lie flat on your back with your feet flat on the ground or resting on a bench with your knees bent at a 90 degree angle.
cue_weighted_crunches_2: Hold a weight to your chest, or you may hold it extended above your torso. This will be your starting position.
cue_weighted_crunches_mistake: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_weighted_dip_1: Lean slightly forward and keep the shoulders down.
cue_weighted_dip_2: Lower until the upper arms are about parallel.
cue_weighted_dip_mistake: Going deeper than the shoulders can control.
cue_weighted_hyperextension_1: Set the pad just below your hip crease so hips hinge freely.
cue_weighted_hyperextension_2: Lower with a flat back and squeeze glutes to rise to straight.
cue_weighted_hyperextension_mistake: Hyperextending past a straight body line at the top.
cue_weighted_jump_squat_1: Position a lightly loaded barbell across the back of your shoulders. You could also use a weighted vest, sandbag, or other type of resistance for this exercise.
cue_weighted_jump_squat_2: The weight should be light enough that it doesn't slow you down significantly. Your feet should be just outside of shoulder width with your head and chest up.
cue_weighted_jump_squat_mistake: Letting knees cave inward or heels lift off the floor.
cue_weighted_pull_up_1: Start from a full hang and pull the chest to the bar.
cue_weighted_pull_up_2: Add weight only once bodyweight reps are clean.
cue_weighted_pull_up_mistake: Cutting the range short as the weight gets heavy.
cue_weighted_push_up_1: Keep a firm line from head to heels under the load.
cue_weighted_push_up_2: Lower the chest toward the floor under control.
cue_weighted_push_up_mistake: Letting the hips sag under the extra weight.
cue_weighted_sissy_squat_1: Standing upright, with feet at shoulder width and toes raised, use one hand to hold onto the beams of a squat rack and the opposite arm to hold a plate on top of your chest.
cue_weighted_sissy_squat_2: As you use one arm to hold yourself, bend at the knees and slowly lower your torso toward the ground by bringing your pelvis and knees forward.
cue_weighted_sissy_squat_mistake: Letting knees cave inward or heels lift off the floor.
cue_weighted_sit_ups_with_bands_1: Start out by strapping the bands around the base of the decline bench.
cue_weighted_sit_ups_with_bands_2: Position your legs through the decline machine until they are secured. Now reach for the exercise bands with both hands.
cue_weighted_sit_ups_with_bands_mistake: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_weighted_squat_1: Start by positioning two flat benches shoulder width apart from each other.
cue_weighted_squat_2: Once you are standing straight up with the weight hanging in between your legs, position your arms so that they are fully extended to the side of your body.
cue_weighted_squat_mistake: Letting knees cave inward or heels lift off the floor.
cue_wide_grip_barbell_curl_1: Grip outside shoulder width with palms facing up.
cue_wide_grip_barbell_curl_2: Keep upper arms still while curling through full range.
cue_wide_grip_barbell_curl_mistake: Flaring elbows outward at the bottom.
cue_wide_grip_bench_press_1: Take a wider grip while keeping shoulder blades tucked down.
cue_wide_grip_bench_press_2: Control the bar to mid-chest and drive feet into the floor.
cue_wide_grip_bench_press_mistake: Flaring elbows at 90 degrees with shrugged shoulders.
cue_wide_grip_decline_barbell_pullover_1: Lie down on a decline bench with both legs securely locked in position. Reach for the barbell behind the head using a pronated grip (palms facing out).
cue_wide_grip_decline_barbell_pullover_2: When positioned properly, your arms should be fully extended and perpendicular to the floor. This is the starting position.
cue_wide_grip_decline_barbell_pullover_m: Pulling with momentum or stopping short of full range.
cue_wide_grip_lat_pulldown_1: Grip outside shoulder width and depress shoulder blades first.
cue_wide_grip_lat_pulldown_2: Pull bar to upper chest with elbows pointing down.
cue_wide_grip_lat_pulldown_mistake: Swinging backward to yank the bar down.
cue_wide_grip_pull_up_1: Grip about one and a half shoulder-widths apart.
cue_wide_grip_pull_up_2: Pull the chest toward the bar, driving the elbows down and out.
cue_wide_grip_pull_up_mistake: Going so wide that the shoulders pinch, or kipping.
cue_wide_grip_pulldown_behind_the_neck_1: Sit down on a pull-down machine with a wide bar attached to the top pulley. Make sure that you adjust the knee pad of the machine to fit your height.
cue_wide_grip_pulldown_behind_the_neck_2: Grab the bar with the palms facing forward using the prescribed grip.
cue_wide_grip_pulldown_behind_the_neck_m: Pulling with momentum or stopping short of full range.
cue_wide_knee_push_up_1: Hands wider than the shoulders, body in one line.
cue_wide_knee_push_up_2: Lower the chest between the hands, slowly.
cue_wide_knee_push_up_mistake: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.
cue_wide_push_up_1: Set hands wider than shoulders, fingers angled slightly out.
cue_wide_push_up_2: Lower under control until chest nears the floor.
cue_wide_push_up_mistake: Flaring elbows straight to 90 degrees or sagging core.
cue_wide_stance_squat_1: Take a wide stance with toes angled out 30 degrees.
cue_wide_stance_squat_2: Push knees out in line with your toes as you sit back.
cue_wide_stance_squat_mistake: Letting knees cave inward out of the bottom.
cue_wind_sprints_1: Hang from a pull-up bar using a pronated grip. Your arms and legs should be extended. This will be your starting position.
cue_wind_sprints_2: Begin by quickly raising one knee as high as you can. Do not swing your body or your legs.
cue_wind_sprints_mistake: Pulling on the neck or using hip momentum.
cue_windmills_1: Lie on your back with your arms extended out to the sides and your legs straight. This will be your starting position.
cue_windmills_2: Lift one leg and quickly cross it over your body, attempting to touch the ground near the opposite hand.
cue_windmills_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_worlds_greatest_stretch_1: This is a three-part stretch. Begin by lunging forward, with your front foot flat on the ground and on the toes of your back foot.
cue_worlds_greatest_stretch_2: Now, place the arm on the same side as your front leg on the ground, with the elbow next to the foot.
cue_worlds_greatest_stretch_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_wrist_circles_1: Start by standing straight with your feet being shoulder width apart from each other.
cue_wrist_circles_2: Keeping your entire body stationary except for the wrists, begin to rotate both wrists forward in a circular motion.
cue_wrist_circles_mistake: Forcing the stretch into sharp pain or bouncing.
cue_wrist_curl_1: Rest the forearms on the thigh and curl the wrists up.
cue_wrist_curl_2: Lower slowly through the full range.
cue_wrist_curl_mistake: Lifting the forearms off the support.
cue_wrist_flexor_stretch_1: Extend the arm palm up and gently pull the fingers back.
cue_wrist_flexor_stretch_2: Keep the elbow straight and the shoulder relaxed.
cue_wrist_flexor_stretch_mistake: Pulling the fingers back too hard.
cue_wrist_roller_1: Hold arms straight out in front at shoulder height.
cue_wrist_roller_2: Roll the weight smoothly up, then control it back down.
cue_wrist_roller_mistake: Letting elbows drop or letting the rope unwind freely.
cue_wrist_rotations_with_straight_bar_1: Hold a barbell with both hands and your palms facing down; hands spaced about shoulder width. This will be your starting position.
cue_wrist_rotations_with_straight_bar_2: Alternating between each of your hands, perform the movement by extending the wrist as though you were rolling up a newspaper.
cue_wrist_rotations_with_straight_bar_mi: Swinging the elbows forward to heave the weight.
cue_zercher_squat_1: Cradle the bar in the crooks of your elbows tight to torso.
cue_zercher_squat_2: Keep elbows high and torso upright throughout the squat.
cue_zercher_squat_mistake: Letting the elbows drop and rounding the upper back.
cue_zottman_curl_1: Curl up with palms facing up, then rotate palms down at the top.
cue_zottman_curl_2: Lower slowly with the overhand grip to train forearms.
cue_zottman_preacher_curl_1: Grab a dumbbell in each hand and place your upper arms on top of the preacher bench or the incline bench.
cue_zottman_preacher_curl_2: As you breathe in, slowly lower the dumbbells keeping the palms down until your upper arm is extended and your biceps are fully stretched.
cue_zottman_preacher_curl_mistake: Swinging the elbows forward to heave the weight.
